title: Horizontal singular closure and two-branch conductor atlas
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, uniformizer $\pi$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X	o S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented with nonempty reduced nodal geometric curve fibres [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Here nodal means every nonsmooth closed point over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $
u:C=X^
u	o X$ be the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Assume it is finite and has an etale covering by common affine charts over $R'$, an etale DVR extension of $R$ with uniformizer $\pi'$, with models $Q=R'[u,v]/(uv)$ or $Q=R'[u,v]/(uv-\pi'^n)$, $n\geq0$, on which $
u$ is respectively the pullback of $\operatorname{Spec}(R'[u]	imes R'[v])	o\operatorname{Spec}Q$ or the identity; over the remaining generic points assume smooth identity charts or the identical split-node description over finite separable extensions of $K$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $N_K$ be the reduced closed subscheme of nonsmooth points of $X_K$, let $N\hookrightarrow X$ be its scheme-theoretic closure (the scheme-theoretic image of $N_K	o X$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]), and put $B=C	imes_XN$. Call a chart persistent if its model is a split node $R'[u,v]/(uv)$ or, over the generic fibre, $K'[u,v]/(uv)$ with $K'/K$ finite separable; in the latter case read $K'$ for $R'$ below. The ideal of $N$ pulls back on a persistent chart to $(u,v)$ and on a smoothing or smooth chart to the unit ideal. On a persistent chart $N$ and $B$ are the pullbacks of $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(R'	imes R')$, with the diagonal map on rings; on all other charts they are empty. In particular $N	o S$ and $B	o S$ are finite etale, $B	o N$ is finite etale of constant degree two, $B\hookrightarrow C$ is a closed immersion into the relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $C\setminus B	o X\setminus N$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion]. The restriction $N	imes_SK=N_K$ is canonical. On the generic fibre its ideal is the conductor: for any affine $\operatorname{Spec}T\subseteq X_K$, with normalization algebra $\overline T$, it is $\{a\in T:a\overline T\subseteq T\}$. These assertions include nonsplit nodes and the empty singular locus; no ordering of global branches is required.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), explicit persistent versus smoothing charts; agent kernel-of-generic-restriction and conductor calculations. Finiteness is the projective finite-fibres criterion, coherent.tex Tag 02OG (lemma-characterize-finite).

proof.text: First identify the generic singular subscheme on the supplied charts. Over a field $F$, the hypersurface $F[u,v]/(uv)$ has dimension one, so its displayed presentation is a relative global complete intersection. Its Jacobian row is $(v,u)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth-jacobian] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], its nonsmooth locus is exactly $V(u,v)$, with reduced structure $\operatorname{Spec}F$. For $uv-a$ with $a\ne0$ both $u,v$ are units, so this locus is empty. The pointwise assertion of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] transfers these loci through the etale chart maps. Smoothness is also detected after extension to geometric fibres by [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change]; thus the description over the finite separable fields in the atlas has the same meaning as nonsmoothness over $K$. Pullbacks of the reduced singular subscheme are reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], and therefore are precisely these reduced closed loci. In particular the pullback of $N_K$ is the zero section on persistent generic charts and empty on all others.

The DVR is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Projectivity gives properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper], hence finite type and quasi-compactness by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. It follows from [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] that $X$ is Noetherian. Its generic fibre and all its closed subschemes are Noetherian too. Consequently the locally closed immersion $N_K\to X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] and [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], $N$ is closed in $X$ and $N_K\to N$ is scheme-theoretically dense: its structure sheaf map is injective. In particular there are no arbitrary choices of a reduced special-fibre structure in this construction.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); closure defined by the kernel.

proof.text: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}P\to X$ be a supplied affine etale chart, and set $N_U=N\times_XU$. The projection $N_U\to N$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to the quasi-compact quasi-separated dense map $N_K\to N$. It says that $N_K\times_XU\to N_U$ is scheme-theoretically dense. Since $N_U$ is a closed subscheme of $U$, its ideal is therefore exactly the kernel of restriction from $\mathcal O_U$ to the generic singular subscheme computed in step 1. This uses the dense-case statement of the cited node, not the more general assertion appearing only in its old proof. Thus closure can be calculated on each chart without assuming that arbitrary nonflat base change preserves an image.

source.place: Tag 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image), applied to the dense factor N_K -> N.

proof.text: On a persistent trait chart write $Q=R'[u,v]/(uv)$ and $J=(u,v)$. The map $Q\to P$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Put $H=P/JP=P\otimes_QR'$; its map to $R'$ on spectra is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], so $H$ is flat over $R'$. The image of $\pi$ is nonzero in the domain $R'$, so multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on $R'$ and therefore on $H$, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Thus $H\to H[1/\pi]$ is injective: an element in its kernel is killed by a power of $\pi$, and repeated injectivity makes it zero. The kernel of $P\to H[1/\pi]$ is consequently $JP$. Step 3 identifies this with the ideal of $N_U$. For a generic-only persistent chart the same calculation has $R'=K'$ and no localization, hence kernel $JP$. On smoothing and smooth charts the generic singular subscheme is empty, so its restriction map has zero target and kernel $P$. This proves all asserted ideal formulas.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), the two displayed models; agent kernel-of-generic-restriction calculation.

proof.text:
On a persistent chart, [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor] gives $Q/J=R'$ and $E/JE=R'\times R'$ for $E=R'[u]\times R'[v]$, with the diagonal map $R'\to R'\times R'$. The assumed normalization chart is $\operatorname{Spec}(P\otimes_QE)$. Therefore, directly by the fibre-product rings,
$$N_U=\operatorname{Spec}H,\qquad B_U=\operatorname{Spec}(H\times H),$$
where $H=P/JP$. The map $B_U\to N_U$ is the disjoint union of two identities. On other charts $N_U$ and $B_U$ are empty. These are pullbacks of exactly the two schemes in the statement, rather than an assertion that an etale chart itself equals the whole model.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), persistent model; explicit conductor quotients in lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor.

proof.text: Each $N_U\to S$ is etale: on persistent charts it is the composite of the etale zero-section base change $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ with the given etale map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ (or the generic open followed by the finite separable field extension, etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]); the empty maps are etale too. Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] for composition and open immersions. The maps $N_U\to N$ form a jointly surjective etale family by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Their disjoint union is a surjective etale map: the disjoint components are an open cover and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] applies. Hence [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] implies that $N\to S$ is etale. Likewise $B_U\to N_U$ is etale, so $B_U\to N$ is etale by composition. Apply the same source descent to the jointly surjective etale cover $\coprod B_U\to B$; this proves $B\to N$ etale, and its composite $B\to S$ etale.

source.place: Tag 036W (lemma-etale-etale-local-source); morphisms.tex Tags 02GO, 02GN, 02GP, etale base change and composition.

proof.text: The map $N\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], since $N$ is closed in the proper $X$. Its fibres are zero-dimensional by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Each fibre is Noetherian: by [pqf-lem-proper-basic] it is of finite type over its residue field, and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] supplies local Noetherianity, with quasi-compactness again from properness. Hence each fibre has finitely many points by [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete]. The base $S$ is locally Noetherian, so [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] gives finiteness of $N\to S$. The map $B\to N$ is a base change of the assumed finite $\nu$: on affine opens this tensors a finite algebra, whose finite generating set still generates after tensoring, so it is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Finiteness of $B\to S$ follows by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Combined with step 6, this proves both finite etale assertions.

For any point of $N$ choose a point of an etale cover $N_U$ above it. The base change of $B\to N$ there is the two-copy cover in step 5, hence has fibre algebra of dimension two. Since $B\to N$ is finite etale, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso] identifies its rank with that fibre dimension and says the rank is unchanged under this base change. Its rank is therefore two at every point of $N$. The map $B\hookrightarrow C$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. On each persistent normalization chart the two origins lie on the two affine lines, smooth over $R'$ by [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor]. The charts are etale over these lines; etale maps are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], and smooth ring maps compose by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] on affine opens. This includes the etale base $R'\to R$. The pointwise assertion of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] descends this smoothness to $C$ at every point of $B$.

source.place: Tag 04MH (lemma-finite-locally-free); descent.tex Tag 036U; models.tex persistent chart of Tag 0CDD.

proof.text: Off $N$, the persistent model is covered by $D(u)$ and $D(v)$. In the equal-constant description $Q\subset R'[u]\times R'[v]$ of [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor], localization at $u$ kills the second factor and gives $Q_u=R'[u,u^{-1}]=E_u$; localization at $v$ similarly gives $Q_v=R'[v,v^{-1}]=E_v$. These identities remain identities after the tensor base change to $P$. On every other chart $\nu$ is the identity by hypothesis. Thus the finite map $C\setminus B\to X\setminus N$ is an isomorphism after the supplied etale cover. Here is descent explicitly: over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the target, write its finite inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}D$. Etale openness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and quasi-compactness allow finitely many affine cover charts $\operatorname{Spec}P_i$ covering $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The ring map $A\to\prod_iP_i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and surjective on spectra, hence faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], the kernel and cokernel of $A\to D$ vanish after this tensor product. They vanish already over $A$ by [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero]. Hence $A\to D$ is an isomorphism and these canonical local inverses give the required global inverse.

source.place: Tag 0CDD persistent normalization chart; agent localization calculation and faithfully flat kernel/cokernel descent.

proof.text: Localize the ideals in step 4 at $\pi$. They become $(u,v)$ on the persistent generic charts and the unit ideal on all other charts, exactly the ideals of $N_K$ from step 1. Thus the canonical closed immersion $N_K\to N\times_SK$ is an isomorphism. Equality is equality of ideal sheaves: on affine opens it is detected by the same faithfully flat cover and vanishing of the quotient module used in step 9. In particular the identification is the restriction of the actual closure, not a selected isomorphism of abstract finite schemes.

source.place: Tag 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image), restriction to the generic open; agent ideal comparison.

proof.text: It remains to identify the generic conductor on every affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}T\subset X_K$. First, $X$ is reduced, as the cited affine-normalization statement requires. An affine ring $T$ of $X_K$ embeds in $T\otimes_K\overline K$, a ring of the reduced geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre], by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; so $T$ is reduced and $T\subseteq\overline T$. On an affine ring $A$ of $X$, flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the same node make $\pi$ a nonzerodivisor, so $A\subseteq A[1/\pi]$ is reduced, and Noetherian by step 2. Normalization commutes with principal localization by [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor]; applying this to inversion of $\pi$ shows that the assumed finite $C_K\to X_K$ is the componentwise normalization. Thus its inverse image over $V$ has algebra $\overline T$. Write $M=\overline T/T$, a finite $T$-module. Its annihilator is exactly $\{a\in T:a\overline T\subseteq T\}$. For a generic affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}P\to V$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identify $M\otimes_TP$ with the quotient of the chart normalization algebra by $P$. On a persistent chart $P$ is etale over $Q=K'[u,v]/(uv)$; with $E=K'[u]\times K'[v]$, this quotient is $(E/Q)\otimes_QP$. The module $E/Q$ is finite by [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor]. Apply [lem-trf-annihilator-finite-flat-base-change] first to $Q\to P$ and then to $T\to P$. Its assertion identifies the conductor extended from $T$ with $(u,v)P$ on persistent charts, since the cited split calculation gives $\operatorname{Ann}_Q(E/Q)=(u,v)$. On identity charts the quotient is zero, so its annihilator is the unit ideal. These are exactly the ideals of $N_K$ already computed. Equality of the two ideals over $T$ follows by faithful flat detection as in step 10. This proves the claimed formula for every $V$.

source.place: Tag 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), finite-module assertion; morphisms.tex normalization localization, Tag 035P.

proof.text: Every assertion used only the supplied jointly surjective etale atlas and equality of canonical ideal sheaves or structural maps. A change of a split-node chart may interchange the two factors of $H\times H$, but preserves its diagonal $H$, the ideal $(u,v)$ and the unordered two-copy cover. Hence the assertions descend for nonsplit nodes without choosing an ordering of branches. If $N_K$ is empty, step 3 has zero restriction target on every chart, so $N=B=\varnothing$ and step 9 gives $C\cong X$. A rank-two assertion over the empty $N$ is vacuous. Thus the empty case is included as well.
